name: Ash Cake
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Sweep a clean spot upon the hot hearth
Put the bread down and cover with hot wood ashes
Wash and wipe dry before it is eaten
Alternatively lay a cabbage-leaf above and below the pone
The bread is thus steamed before it is baked, and is made ready for eating by stripping off the leaves

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Mix as for corn-meal pone
2. Sweep a clean spot upon the hot hearth
3. Put the bread down and cover with hot wood ashes
4. Wash and wipe dry before it is eaten
5. Alternatively lay a cabbage-leaf above and below the pone
6. The bread is thus steamed before it is baked, and is made ready for eating by stripping off the leaves
